isl:1990:10.text: A plane tangent to the circumference of the base of a right circular cone passes through the midpoint of its altitude and cuts the cone into two parts. Find the volume of the smaller part as a fraction of the cone's volume.
isl:1990:10.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1990:10.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1990:11.text: Chords $AB,CD$ of a circle meet at $E$. Choose $M$ on chord $AB$, with $M\ne E$, and draw the circle through $D,E,M$. Its tangent at $E$ meets lines $BC,AC$ at $F,G$. Given $AM/AB=\lambda$, determine $GE/EF$.
isl:1990:11.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1990:11.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1990:12.text: Through $C$ of triangle $ABC$, draw line $L\parallel AB$. The internal bisector at $A$ meets $BC,L$ at $D,E$, respectively; the internal bisector at $B$ meets $AC,L$ at $F,G$. If $GF=DE$, prove that $AC=BC$.
isl:1990:12.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1990:12.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1990:19.text: Let $P$ be inside a regular tetrahedron $T$ of volume $1$. The four planes through $P$ parallel to its faces partition $T$ into $14$ pieces. Let $f(P)$ be the total volume of the pieces which are neither tetrahedra nor parallelepipeds—that is, pieces adjacent to an edge but not a vertex. Determine the exact bounds of $f(P)$ as $P$ varies in $T$.
isl:1990:19.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1990:19.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1990:5.text: Triangle $ABC$ is scalene. Let $G,K,H$ be its centroid, incenter, and orthocenter. Prove that $\angle GKH>90^\circ$.
isl:1990:5.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1990:5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1990:9.text: Triangle $ABC$ has incenter $K$. Let $C_1,B_1$ be the midpoints of $AB,AC$. Put $B_2=C_1K\cap AC$ and $C_2=B_1K\cap AB$. If triangles $AB_2C_2$ and $ABC$ have equal areas, determine $\angle CAB$.
isl:1990:9.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1990:9.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1991:1.text: Let $P$ be inside triangle $ABC$. Drop perpendiculars from $P$ to $AC,BC$, with feet $P_1,P_2$. Drop perpendiculars from $C$ to $AP,BP$, with feet $Q_1,Q_2$. Prove that $Q_1P_2,Q_2P_1,AB$ are concurrent.
isl:1991:1.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1991:1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1991:2.text: In an acute triangle $ABC$, let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and take $P\in AM$ with $PM=BM$. Let $H$ be the perpendicular projection of $P$ onto $BC$. The perpendicular to $PB$ through $H$ meets segment $AB$ at $Q$, and the perpendicular to $PC$ through $H$ meets segment $AC$ at $R$. Prove that the circumcircle of $QHR$ is tangent to $BC$ at $H$.
isl:1991:2.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1991:2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1991:3.text:
For a point $S$ on the circumcircle of triangle $PQR$, denote its Simson line—the line through its perpendicular projections onto the three sidelines—by $\ell(S,PQR)$. A hexagon $ABCDEF$ is inscribed in a circle. Prove that
$$\ell(A,BDF),\quad\ell(B,ACE),\quad\ell(D,ABF),\quad\ell(E,ABC)$$
are concurrent if and only if $CDEF$ is a rectangle.
isl:1991:3.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1991:3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1991:4.text: For a point $M$ inside triangle $ABC$, prove that at least one of $\angle MAB,\angle MBC,\angle MCA$ is at most $30^\circ$.
isl:1991:4.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1991:4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1991:5.text: Triangle $ABC$ has $\angle A=60^\circ$ and incenter $I$. The parallel to $AC$ through $I$ meets side $AB$ at $F$. Choose $P\in BC$ with $3BP=BC$. Prove that $\angle BFP=\tfrac12\angle B$.
isl:1991:5.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1991:5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1991:6.text:
Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$, and let $\ell_A,\ell_B,\ell_C$ be its internal angle-bisector lengths. Prove that
$$\frac14<\frac{IA\cdot IB\cdot IC}{\ell_A\ell_B\ell_C}\leq\frac8{27}.$$
isl:1991:6.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1991:6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1991:7.text:
Let $O$ be the circumsphere center of tetrahedron $ABCD$, and let $L,M,N$ be the midpoints of $BC,CA,AB$. Suppose
$$AB+BC=AD+CD,\quad BC+CA=BD+AD,\quad CA+AB=CD+BD.$$
Prove that $\angle LOM=\angle MON=\angle NOL$.
isl:1991:7.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1991:7.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1992:CHN-2.text:
A quadrilateral $ABCD$ has $AC\perp BD$. Erect squares $ABEF,BCGH,CDIJ,DAKL$ externally on its sides, with the vertices in the indicated cyclic orders. Define
$$P_1=CL\cap DF,\quad Q_1=DF\cap AH,\quad R_1=AH\cap BJ,\quad S_1=BJ\cap CL,$$
and
$$P_2=AI\cap BK,\quad Q_2=BK\cap CE,\quad R_2=CE\cap DG,\quad S_2=DG\cap AI.$$
Prove that quadrilaterals $P_1Q_1R_1S_1$ and $P_2Q_2R_2S_2$ are congruent.
isl:1992:CHN-2.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1992:CHN-2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1992:COL-3.text: A convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ has $AC=BD$. Erect equilateral triangles externally on its four sides, and let $O_1,O_2,O_3,O_4$ be their centers for sides $AB,BC,CD,DA$, respectively. Prove that $O_1O_3\perp O_2O_4$.
isl:1992:COL-3.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1992:COL-3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1992:COL-3.sourceCaveat: External orientation is made explicit from Figure9 of the supplied organizer scan (combined PDF physical18); the printed prose alone leaves the orientation implicit.

isl:1992:FRA1.text: A circle $C$ is tangent to a line $\ell$, and $M$ is a fixed point of $\ell$. Find the locus of points $P$ for which points $Q,R\in\ell$ exist such that $M$ is the midpoint of $QR$ and $C$ is the incircle of triangle $PQR$.
isl:1992:FRA1.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1992:FRA1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1992:FRA1.sourceAlias: FRA 1 / SL92-20 supplementary entry, absent from the initial18-item organizer table
isl:1992:FRA1.sourceCaveat: Compendium-attributed supplementary provenance; no independently obtained original organizer supplement is claimed.

isl:1992:IND-4.text: Circles $G_1,G_2$ touch externally at $W$ and are both internally tangent to a circle $G$. Choose $A,B,C$ on $G$ so that line $BC$ is a common direct tangent of $G_1,G_2$, and line $WA$ is their common transverse tangent at $W$. Assume $W,A$ lie on the same side of $BC$. Prove that $W$ is the incenter of $ABC$.
isl:1992:IND-4.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1992:IND-4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1992:JPN-2.text: In triangle $ABC$, the internal bisectors of $\angle ABC,\angle ACB$ meet $AC,AB$ at $D,E$, respectively. If $\angle BDE=24^\circ$ and $\angle CED=18^\circ$, determine $\angle A,\angle B,\angle C$.
isl:1992:JPN-2.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1992:JPN-2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1992:JPN-2.sourceAlias: JAP 2 in the Compendium; JPN-2 / SL92-11 in the preserved organizer inventory

isl:1993:CAN2.text:
Triangle $ABC$ has circumradius $1$ and inradius $r$. Let $p$ be the inradius of its orthic triangle, whose vertices are the feet of its altitudes. Prove that
$$p\leq1-\frac{(1+r)^2}{3}.$$
isl:1993:CAN2.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1993:CAN2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1993:ESP1.text: Triangle $ABC$ has circumcircle $k$ centered at $O$ with radius $R$, and incircle centered at $I$ with radius $r$. Another circle $k_c$ touches sides $CA,CB$ at $D,E$ and touches $k$ internally. Prove that $I$ is the midpoint of $DE$.
isl:1993:ESP1.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1993:ESP1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1993:ESP1.sourceAlias: SPA 1 in the Compendium; ESP1 in the preserved organizer list

isl:1993:ESP2.text:
Choose $D,E$ on side $BC$ of triangle $ABC$ with $\angle BAD=\angle CAE$. Let $M,N$ be the points where the incircles of $ABD,ACE$ touch $BC$. Prove that
$$\frac1{MB}+\frac1{MD}=\frac1{NC}+\frac1{NE}.$$
isl:1993:ESP2.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1993:ESP2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1993:ESP2.sourceAlias: SPA 2 in the Compendium; ESP2 in the preserved organizer list

isl:1993:ISA1.text:
The vertices $D,E,F$ of an equilateral triangle lie on sides $BC,CA,AB$ of triangle $ABC$. If those sides have lengths $a,b,c$ and $ABC$ has area $S$, prove that
$$DE\geq\frac{2\sqrt2\,S}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2+4\sqrt3\,S}}.$$
isl:1993:ISA1.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1993:ISA1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1993:ISA1.sourceAlias: ISR 1 in the Compendium; ISA1 in the organizer scan (physical52 of the combined scan)

isl:1993:MAK1.text:
For points $A,B,C$ in the plane, let $m(ABC)$ be the least altitude of triangle $ABC$, taking $m(ABC)=0$ if the points are collinear. Prove that for every point $X$,
$$m(ABC)\leq m(ABX)+m(AXC)+m(XBC).$$
isl:1993:MAK1.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1993:MAK1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1993:MAK1.sourceAlias: MCD 1 in the Compendium; MAK1 in the preserved organizer list

isl:1993:UNK1.text: Say that a circle $S$ cuts a circle $\Sigma$ diametrally when their common chord is a diameter of $\Sigma$. Let $S_A,S_B,S_C$ be circles with distinct centers $A,B,C$. Prove that $A,B,C$ are collinear if and only if there is no unique circle cutting all three diametrally. If more than one such circle exists, prove that they all pass through two fixed points and locate these points relative to $S_A,S_B,S_C$.
isl:1993:UNK1.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1993:UNK1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1993:UNK1.sourceAlias: GBR 1 in the Compendium; UNK1 in the preserved organizer list

isl:1993:UNK2.text:
Points $C,D$ lie on the same side of line $AB$, and
$$AC\cdot BD=AD\cdot BC,\qquad\angle ADB=90^\circ+\angle ACB.$$
Find $AB\cdot CD/(AC\cdot BD)$, and prove that the circles $ACD,BCD$ are orthogonal: their tangents at each intersection are perpendicular.
isl:1993:UNK2.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1993:UNK2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1993:UNK2.sourceAlias: GBR 2 in the Compendium; UNK2 in the preserved organizer list

isl:1994:G1.text: A semicircle $\Gamma$ lies on one side of line $\ell$. At points $C,D$ of its arc, the tangents meet $\ell$ at $B,A$, respectively, with the semicircle's center between $A,B$. Put $E=AC\cap BD$, and let $F$ be the perpendicular projection of $E$ onto $\ell$. Prove that $EF$ bisects $\angle CFD$.
isl:1994:G1.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1994:G1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1994:G2.text: A quadrilateral $ABCD$ has $BC\parallel AD$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $CD$, $P$ the midpoint of $MA$, and $Q$ the midpoint of $MB$. If $N=DP\cap CQ$, prove that $N$ is not outside triangle $ABM$.
isl:1994:G2.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1994:G2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1994:G2.sourceCaveat: Literal printed claim retained but NOT ready to publish: the Compendium footnote explicitly says it is false as stated, and becomes true if triangle ABM is replaced by quadrilateral ABCD. Reconcile the chosen version with any future classification before attachment; no silent correction.

isl:1994:G3.text: A circle $\omega$ touches parallel lines $\ell_1,\ell_2$. Circle $\omega_1$ touches $\ell_1$ at $A$ and $\omega$ externally at $C$. Circle $\omega_2$ touches $\ell_2$ at $B$, $\omega$ externally at $D$, and $\omega_1$ externally at $E$. If $Q=AD\cap BC$, prove that $Q$ is the circumcenter of $CDE$.
isl:1994:G3.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1994:G3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1994:G4.text: Let $N$ be any point on the internal bisector of $\angle BAC$. Choose $P$ on line $AB$ and $O$ on line $AN$ so that $\angle ANP=\angle APO=90^\circ$. A line through a point $Q$ on $NP$ meets lines $AB,AC$ at $E,F$. Prove that $\angle OQE=90^\circ$ if and only if $QE=QF$.
isl:1994:G4.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1994:G4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1994:G5.text: A line $\ell$ does not meet a circle $\omega$ centered at $O$. Let $E$ be the perpendicular projection of $O$ onto $\ell$, and take $M\in\ell$, $M\ne E$. The tangents from $M$ touch $\omega$ at $A,B$. Drop perpendiculars from $E$ to $MA,MB$, with feet $C,D$. Prove that $F=CD\cap OE$ is independent of $M$.
isl:1994:G5.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1994:G5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1995:G1.text: Distinct collinear points $A,B,C,D$ occur in that order. The circles with diameters $AC,BD$ meet at $X,Y$. Choose $O$ on line $XY$ but off line $AD$. Lines $CO,BO$ meet the respective circles again at $M,N$. Prove that $AM,DN,XY$ are concurrent.
isl:1995:G1.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1995:G1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1995:G2.text:
For noncollinear points $A,B,C$, prove that exactly one point $X$ in their plane satisfies
$$XA^2+XB^2+AB^2=XB^2+XC^2+BC^2=XC^2+XA^2+CA^2.$$
isl:1995:G2.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1995:G2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1995:G3.text: The incircle of $ABC$ touches $BC,CA,AB$ at $D,E,F$. A point $X$ inside $ABC$ has the property that the incircle of $XBC$ also touches $BC$ at $D$; it touches $CX,XB$ at $Y,Z$. Prove that $E,F,Z,Y$ are concyclic.
isl:1995:G3.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1995:G3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1995:G4.text:
In an acute triangle $ABC$, choose $A_1,A_2$ on $BC$ with $A_2$ between $A_1,C$; $B_1,B_2$ on $CA$ with $B_2$ between $B_1,A$; and $C_1,C_2$ on $AB$ with $C_2$ between $C_1,B$. Suppose
$$\angle AA_1A_2=\angle AA_2A_1=\angle BB_1B_2=\angle BB_2B_1=\angle CC_1C_2=\angle CC_2C_1.$$
Lines $AA_1,BB_1,CC_1$ form one triangle, and $AA_2,BB_2,CC_2$ form another. Prove that their six vertices lie on a circle.
isl:1995:G4.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1995:G4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1995:G5.text:
A convex hexagon $ABCDEF$ satisfies $AB=BC=CD$, $DE=EF=FA$, and $\angle BCD=\angle EFA=60^\circ$. Interior points $G,H$ satisfy $\angle AGB=\angle DHE=120^\circ$. Prove that
$$AG+GB+GH+DH+HE\geq CF.$$
isl:1995:G5.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1995:G5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1995:G6.text:
Let $G$ be the centroid of tetrahedron $A_1A_2A_3A_4$. For each $i$, let $A_i'$ be the intersection other than $A_i$ of line $GA_i$ with the circumsphere. Prove that
$$GA_1\,GA_2\,GA_3\,GA_4\leq GA_1'\,GA_2'\,GA_3'\,GA_4'$$
and
$$\frac1{GA_1'}+\frac1{GA_2'}+\frac1{GA_3'}+\frac1{GA_4'}\leq\frac1{GA_1}+\frac1{GA_2}+\frac1{GA_3}+\frac1{GA_4}.$$
isl:1995:G6.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1995:G6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1995:G6.sourceCaveat: The second sphere intersections distinct from the original vertices are made explicit; no replacement of lines by outward rays is intended.

isl:1995:G7.text:
Let $O$ be inside a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ of area $S$. Points $K,L,M,N$ lie inside sides $AB,BC,CD,DA$, respectively. If $OKBL$ and $OMDN$ are parallelograms, prove that
$$\sqrt S\geq\sqrt{S_1}+\sqrt{S_2},$$
where $S_1,S_2$ are the areas of $ONAK,OLCM$.
isl:1995:G7.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1995:G7.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1995:G8.text: A circle through $B,C$ meets sides $AB,AC$ of triangle $ABC$ again at $C',B'$. If $H,H'$ are the orthocenters of $ABC,AB'C'$, respectively, prove that $BB',CC',HH'$ are concurrent.
isl:1995:G8.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1995:G8.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1996:G1.text: Let $H$ be the orthocenter of triangle $ABC$, and let $P$ lie on its circumcircle, distinct from $A,B,C$. Let $E$ be the foot of altitude $BH$. Construct parallelograms $PAQB$ and $PARC$, and put $X=AQ\cap HR$. Prove that $EX\parallel AP$.
isl:1996:G1.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1996:G1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1996:G2.text:
An interior point $P$ of triangle $ABC$ satisfies
$$\angle APB-\angle C=\angle APC-\angle B.$$
Let $D,E$ be the incenters of $APB,APC$, respectively. Prove that $AP,BD,CE$ are concurrent.
isl:1996:G2.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1996:G2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1996:G3.text: In an acute triangle $ABC$, suppose $BC>CA$. Let $O,H$ be its circumcenter and orthocenter, and let $F$ be the foot of altitude $CH$. The perpendicular to $OF$ through $F$ meets side $CA$ at $P$. Prove that $\angle FHP=\angle BAC$.
isl:1996:G3.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1996:G3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1996:G3.sourceCaveat: The source separately suggests an optional extension asking what happens for BC<=CA; it is not treated as another original problem.

isl:1996:G4.text:
Let $P$ be inside an equilateral triangle $ABC$. Lines $AP,BP,CP$ meet $BC,CA,AB$ at $A_1,B_1,C_1$. Prove that
$$A_1B_1\cdot B_1C_1\cdot C_1A_1\geq A_1B\cdot B_1C\cdot C_1A.$$
isl:1996:G4.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1996:G4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1996:G5.text: A convex hexagon $ABCDEF$ has $AB\parallel DE$, $BC\parallel EF$, $CD\parallel AF$. Let $R_A,R_C,R_E$ be the circumradii of $FAB,BCD,DEF$, respectively, and let $P$ be the hexagon's perimeter. Prove that $R_A+R_C+R_E\geq P/2$.
isl:1996:G5.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1996:G5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1996:G6.text:
Two rectangles have side lengths $a,b$ and $c,d$, where $a<c\leq d<b$ and $ab<cd$. Prove that the first rectangle can be placed inside the second if and only if
$$(b^2-a^2)^2\leq(bd-ac)^2+(bc-ad)^2.$$
isl:1996:G6.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1996:G6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1996:G7.text:
An acute triangle $ABC$ has circumcenter $O$ and circumradius $R$. Lines $AO,BO,CO$ meet the circles $BOC,COA,AOB$ again at $A',B',C'$, respectively. Prove that
$$OA'\cdot OB'\cdot OC'\geq8R^3,$$
and determine when equality holds.
isl:1996:G7.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1996:G7.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1996:G8.text:
In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$, denote the circumradii of $DAB,ABC,BCD,CDA$ by $R_A,R_B,R_C,R_D$, respectively. Prove that
$$R_A+R_C>R_B+R_D\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\angle A+\angle C>\angle B+\angle D.$$
isl:1996:G8.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1996:G8.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1996:G9.text: Let $F$ be a polygon in the plane, not necessarily convex, and $O$ a point. Let $P$ be the perimeter of $F$, $D$ the sum of the distances from $O$ to its vertices, and $H$ the sum of the distances from $O$ to the lines containing its sides. Prove that $D^2-H^2\geq P^2/4$.
isl:1996:G9.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1996:G9.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1997:P16.text: In an acute triangle $ABC$, let $AD,BE$ be altitudes and $AP,BQ$ internal angle bisectors. Let $I,O$ be the incenter and circumcenter. Prove that $D,E,I$ are collinear if and only if $P,Q,O$ are collinear.
isl:1997:P16.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1997:P16.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1997:P18.text: The altitudes from $A,B,C$ of an acute triangle $ABC$ have feet $D,E,F$ on the opposite sides. The parallel to $EF$ through $D$ meets lines $AC,AB$ at $Q,R$. Put $P=EF\cap BC$. Prove that the circumcircle of $PQR$ passes through the midpoint of $BC$.

isl:1997:P20.text: Choose $D$ inside side $BC$ of triangle $ABC$, and let $AD$ meet its circumcircle again at $X$. Let $P,Q$ be the perpendicular projections of $X$ onto $AB,AC$, and let $\gamma$ have diameter $XD$. Prove that $PQ$ is tangent to $\gamma$ if and only if $AB=AC$.

isl:1997:P23.text:
In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$, let $O=AC\cap BD$. Suppose
$$OA\sin\angle A+OC\sin\angle C=OB\sin\angle B+OD\sin\angle D.$$
Prove that $ABCD$ is cyclic.

isl:1997:P25.text: The internal bisectors of $\angle A,\angle B,\angle C$ of triangle $ABC$ meet the circumcircle again at $K,L,M$, respectively. Choose $R$ inside side $AB$. Define $P$ by $RP\parallel AK$ and $BP\perp BL$, and define $Q$ by $RQ\parallel BL$ and $AQ\perp AK$. Prove that $KP,LQ,MR$ are concurrent.

isl:1997:P5.text: Let $ABCD$ be a regular tetrahedron. Take distinct points $M,N$ in the planes $ABC,ADC$, respectively. Prove that $MN,BN,MD$ are the side lengths of a triangle.

isl:1997:P7.text:
A convex hexagon $ABCDEF$ satisfies $AB=BC$, $CD=DE$, and $EF=FA$. Prove that
$$\frac{BC}{BE}+\frac{DE}{DA}+\frac{FA}{FC}\geq\frac32,$$
and determine when equality holds.
isl:1997:P7.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium compiled shortlist reproduction; organizer-original provenance distinguished
isl:1997:P7.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.

isl:1997:P8.text:
Four distinct points $A,B,C,D$ lie on a circle $\Gamma$, and triangle $BCD$ is not right-angled. Prove that:
(a) The perpendicular bisectors of $AB,AC$ meet line $AD$ at points $W,V$, respectively, and lines $CV,BW$ meet at a point $T$.
(b) One of $AD,BT,CT$ equals the sum of the other two.

Original shortlist formulation supplied in the same source: in triangle $ABC$, $\angle A$ is the smallest. A line through $A$ meets the circumcircle again at $U$ on the arc $BC$ opposite $A$. The perpendicular bisectors of $CA,AB$ meet $AU$ at $V,W$, respectively, and $T=CV\cap BW$. Prove that $AU=TB+TC$.

isl:1997:P8.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete printed statement.
isl:1997:P8.sourceCaveat: Both the contest formulation and the explicitly identified original shortlist formulation are retained from the source.

isl:1997:P9.text: Let $A_1A_2A_3$ be a nonisosceles triangle with incenter $I$. For each $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, let $C_i$ be the smaller circle through $I$ tangent to the two sidelines through $A_i$. Let $B_i$ be the intersection other than $I$ of the two circles among $C_1,C_2,C_3$ whose indices differ from $i$. Prove that the circumcenters of $A_1B_1I,A_2B_2I,A_3B_3I$ are collinear.

isl:1998:G1.text: A convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ has perpendicular diagonals. The perpendicular bisectors of $AB,CD$ meet at a unique interior point $P$. Prove that $ABCD$ is cyclic if and only if triangles $ABP,CDP$ have equal areas.

isl:1998:G2.text: In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, points $E\in AB,F\in CD$ vary with $AE:EB=CF:FD$. Choose $P$ on segment $EF$ with $PE:PF=AB:CD$. Prove that the ratio of the areas of triangles $APD,BPC$ is independent of $E,F$.

isl:1998:G3.text: The incircle of triangle $ABC$, centered at $I$, touches $AB,BC,CA$ at $K,L,M$, respectively. Draw line $t$ through $B$ parallel to $KL$, and put $R=MK\cap t$, $S=ML\cap t$. Prove that $\angle RIS$ is acute.

isl:1998:G4.text:
Interior points $M,N$ of triangle $ABC$ satisfy $\angle MAB=\angle NAC$ and $\angle MBA=\angle NBC$. Prove that
$$\frac{AM\cdot AN}{AB\cdot AC}+\frac{BM\cdot BN}{BA\cdot BC}+\frac{CM\cdot CN}{CA\cdot CB}=1.$$

isl:1998:G5.text: Let $H,O,R$ be the orthocenter, circumcenter, and circumradius of triangle $ABC$. Reflect $A,B,C$ in lines $BC,CA,AB$ to obtain $D,E,F$, respectively. Prove that $D,E,F$ are collinear if and only if $OH=2R$.

isl:1998:G6.text:
A convex hexagon $ABCDEF$ satisfies $\angle B+\angle D+\angle F=360^\circ$ and
$$\frac{AB}{BC}\cdot\frac{CD}{DE}\cdot\frac{EF}{FA}=1.$$
Prove that
$$\frac{BC}{CA}\cdot\frac{AE}{EF}\cdot\frac{FD}{DB}=1.$$

isl:1998:G7.text: In triangle $ABC$, suppose $\angle ACB=2\angle ABC$. Choose $D\in BC$ with $CD=2BD$, and extend $AD$ beyond $D$ to $E$ with $AD=DE$. Prove that $\angle ECB+180^\circ=2\angle EBC$.

isl:1998:G8.text: Triangle $ABC$ has $\angle A=90^\circ$ and $\angle B<\angle C$. Its circumcircle $\omega$ has tangent at $A$ meeting line $BC$ at $D$. Reflect $A$ in $BC$ to get $E$, let $X$ be the perpendicular projection of $A$ onto $BE$, and let $Y$ be the midpoint of $AX$. If $BY$ meets $\omega$ again at $Z$, prove that $BD$ is tangent to the circumcircle of $ADZ$.

isl:1999:G2.text: For a set of five points in the plane, call a circle a separator if it passes through three of the points, has a fourth strictly inside, and the fifth strictly outside. Prove that every five-point set with no three collinear and no four concyclic has exactly four separators.

isl:1999:G3.text: A set $S$ of at least three points in three-dimensional space is called completely symmetric if, for any distinct $A,B\in S$, reflection in the perpendicular-bisector plane of $AB$ preserves $S$. Prove that every finite completely symmetric set consists of the vertices of a regular polygon, a regular tetrahedron, or a regular octahedron.

isl:1999:G4.text: In a triangle $T=ABC$, choose $X$ on side $AB$ with $AX/XB=4/5$, then choose $Y$ on segment $CX$ with $CY=2YX$. If possible, choose $Z$ on ray $CA$ such that $\angle CXZ=180^\circ-\angle ABC$. Let $\Sigma$ be the set of triangles $T$ for which $\angle XYZ=45^\circ$. Prove that all triangles in $\Sigma$ are similar, and find their smallest angle.

The common chord line of $\Omega_1,\Omega_2$ meets $\Omega$ at $A,B$. Lines $MA,MB$ meet $\Omega_1$ again at $C,D$. Prove that $\Omega_2$ is tangent to $CD$.

isl:2000:G2.text: Circles $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ meet at $M,N$. A common tangent touches them at $A,B$, labeled so that $M$ is nearer line $AB$ than $N$. The parallel to $AB$ through $M$ meets $\Gamma_1$ again at $C$ and $\Gamma_2$ again at $D$. Put $E=AC\cap BD$, $P=AN\cap CD$, and $Q=BN\cap CD$. Prove that $EP=EQ$.

isl:2001:G3.text:
Let $G$ be the centroid of triangle $ABC$. Find, with proof, the point $P$ in the plane that minimizes
$$AP\cdot AG+BP\cdot BG+CP\cdot CG,$$

isl:2001:G4.text:
For an interior point $M$ of triangle $ABC$, let $A',B',C'$ be its perpendicular projections onto $BC,CA,AB$. Define
$$p(M)=\frac{MA'\cdot MB'\cdot MC'}{MA\cdot MB\cdot MC}.$$
Determine, with proof, where $M$ must lie to maximize $p(M)$. If $\mu(ABC)$ denotes that maximum, determine which triangles maximize $\mu(ABC)$.

Outside an acute triangle $ABC$, construct isosceles triangles $DAC,EAB,FBC$ with $DA=DC$, $EA=EB$, $FB=FC$, and
$$\angle ADC=2\angle BAC,\quad \angle BEA=2\angle ABC,\quad \angle CFB=2\angle ACB.$$
Put $D'=DB\cap EF$, $E'=EC\cap DF$, and $F'=FA\cap DE$. Find, with proof,

isl:2003:G3.text:
For an interior point $P$ of triangle $ABC$, let $D,E,F$ be its perpendicular projections onto $BC,CA,AB$. Suppose
$$AP^2+PD^2=BP^2+PE^2=CP^2+PF^2.$$
If $I_A,I_B,I_C$ are the excenters of $ABC$, prove that $P$ is the circumcenter of $I_AI_BI_C$.
isl:2003:G3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete source statement.
isl:2003:G3.sourceLabel: Attributed reproduction of the 2003 shortlist booklet hosted by the IMO Compendium

isl:2003:G4.text:
Four distinct circles $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2,\Gamma_3,\Gamma_4$ have the following properties. Circles $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_3$ touch externally at $P$, and $\Gamma_2,\Gamma_4$ also touch externally at $P$. The other intersection points of consecutive pairs $(\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)$, $(\Gamma_2,\Gamma_3)$, $(\Gamma_3,\Gamma_4)$, $(\Gamma_4,\Gamma_1)$ are $A,B,C,D$, respectively, all distinct from $P$. Prove that
$$\frac{AB\cdot BC}{AD\cdot DC}=\frac{PB^2}{PD^2}.$$
isl:2003:G4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete source statement.
isl:2003:G4.sourceLabel: Attributed reproduction of the 2003 shortlist booklet hosted by the IMO Compendium

isl:2003:G5.text: Let $AC=BC$ in triangle $ABC$, whose incenter is $I$. Choose $P$ on the circumcircle of $AIB$ inside $ABC$. The parallels to $CA,CB$ through $P$ meet $AB$ at $D,E$, respectively; the parallel to $AB$ through $P$ meets $CA,CB$ at $F,G$. Prove that $DF$ and $EG$ meet on the circumcircle of $ABC$.
isl:2003:G5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete source statement.
isl:2003:G5.sourceLabel: Attributed reproduction of the 2003 shortlist booklet hosted by the IMO Compendium

isl:2003:G6.text: In a convex hexagon, each pair of opposite sides satisfies this condition: the distance between their midpoints equals $\sqrt3/2$ times the sum of their lengths. Prove that all six interior angles of the hexagon are equal.
isl:2003:G6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete source statement.
isl:2003:G6.sourceLabel: Attributed reproduction of the 2003 shortlist booklet hosted by the IMO Compendium

isl:2003:G7.text:
Let a triangle $ABC$ have semiperimeter $s$ and inradius $r$. Draw semicircles with diameters $BC,CA,AB$ outside the triangle. If the circle tangent to all three semicircles has radius $t$, prove that
$$\frac{s}{2}<t\leq\frac{s}{2}+\left(1-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)r.$$
isl:2003:G7.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; matched to the complete source statement.
isl:2003:G7.sourceLabel: Attributed reproduction of the 2003 shortlist booklet hosted by the IMO Compendium

isl:2004:G1.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB\ne AC$. The circle with diameter $BC$ meets $AB,AC$ at $M,N$, respectively. Let $O$ be the midpoint of $BC$, and let $R$ be the intersection of the bisectors of $\angle BAC$ and $\angle MON$. Prove that the circumcircles of $BMR,CNR$ have a common point on segment $BC$.
isl:2004:G1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2004:G1.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2004 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2004:G2.text: A circle $\Gamma$ is disjoint from a line $\ell$. Its diameter $AB$ is perpendicular to $\ell$, with $B$ nearer the line. Choose $C\in\Gamma\setminus\{A,B\}$, and put $D=AC\cap\ell$. Draw the tangent $DE$ to $\Gamma$ so that $B,E$ lie on the same side of $AC$. Set $F=BE\cap\ell$, and let $AF$ meet $\Gamma$ again at $G\ne A$. Prove that the reflection of $G$ in $AB$ lies on $CF$.
isl:2004:G2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2004:G2.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2004 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2004:G3.text: An acute triangle $ABC$ has circumcenter $O$ and $\angle B<\angle C$. Put $D=AO\cap BC$, and let $E,F$ be the circumcenters of $ABD,ACD$. On rays $BA,CA$ beyond $A$, choose $G,H$ with $AG=AC$ and $AH=AB$. Prove that $EFGH$ is a rectangle if and only if $\angle ACB-\angle ABC=60^\circ$.
isl:2004:G3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2004:G3.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2004 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2004:G4.text: In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$, diagonal $BD$ bisects neither $\angle ABC$ nor $\angle CDA$. An interior point $P$ satisfies $\angle PBC=\angle DBA$ and $\angle PDC=\angle BDA$. Prove that $ABCD$ is cyclic if and only if $AP=CP$.
isl:2004:G4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2004:G4.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2004 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2004:G5.text:
Let $A_1A_2\dots A_n$ be a regular $n$-gon. Define points $B_i$ on $A_iA_{i+1}$ for $1\leq i\leq n-1$. Set $B_1,B_{n-1}$ to be the midpoints of their respective sides. For $2\leq i\leq n-2$, put $S=A_1A_{i+1}\cap A_nA_i$ and let $B_i$ be where the bisector of $\angle A_iSA_{i+1}$ meets $A_iA_{i+1}$. Prove that
$$\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\angle A_1B_iA_n=180^\circ.$$
isl:2004:G5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2004:G5.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2004 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2004:G6.text: Prove that every convex polygon contains a convex hexagon whose area is at least three quarters of the polygon's area.
isl:2004:G6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2004:G6.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2004 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2004:G7.text: For a fixed triangle $ABC$, a point $X$ varies on line $BC$ beyond $C$, with $C$ between $B,X$. Suppose the incircles of $ABX,ACX$ meet at two distinct points $P,Q$. Prove that line $PQ$ always passes through a fixed point independent of $X$.
isl:2004:G7.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2004:G7.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2004 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2004:G8.text: In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, let $E=AD\cap BC$, with $C$ between $B,E$, and let $F=AC\cap BD$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $CD$. Choose $N\ne M$ on the circumcircle of $ABM$ with $AN/BN=AM/BM$. Prove that $E,F,N$ are collinear.
isl:2004:G8.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2004:G8.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2004 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2005:G1.text: Triangle $ABC$ satisfies $AB+BC=3AC$. Its incircle, centered at $I$, touches $AB,BC$ at $D,E$. Reflect $D,E$ in $I$ to obtain $K,L$, respectively. Prove that $A,C,K,L$ are concyclic.
isl:2005:G1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2005:G1.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2005 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2005:G2.text: Points $A_1,A_2$ on $BC$, $B_1,B_2$ on $CA$, and $C_1,C_2$ on $AB$ of an equilateral triangle $ABC$ form a convex hexagon $A_1A_2B_1B_2C_1C_2$ with all six sides equal. Prove that $A_1B_2,B_1C_2,C_1A_2$ meet at one point.
isl:2005:G2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2005:G2.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2005 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2005:G3.text: In a parallelogram $ABCD$, a variable line $\ell$ through $A$ meets rays $BC,DC$ at $X,Y$, respectively. Let $K,L$ be the excenters of $ABX,ADY$ corresponding to sides $BX,DY$. Prove that $\angle KCL$ is independent of $\ell$.
isl:2005:G3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2005:G3.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2005 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2005:G4.text: Fix a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $BC=AD$ and $BC$ not parallel to $AD$. Choose interior points $E\in BC,F\in AD$ with $BE=DF$. Put $P=AC\cap BD$, $Q=BD\cap EF$, and $R=EF\cap AC$. Prove that, as $E,F$ vary, all circumcircles of the resulting triangles $PQR$ share a fixed point other than $P$.
isl:2005:G4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2005:G4.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2005 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2005:G5.text: Let $ABC$ be acute with $AB\ne AC$, let $H$ be its orthocenter, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Points $D\in AB,E\in AC$ satisfy $AD=AE$, and $D,H,E$ are collinear. Prove that $HM$ is perpendicular to the common chord of the circumcircles of $ABC$ and $ADE$.
isl:2005:G5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2005:G5.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2005 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2005:G6.text: The median $AM$ of triangle $ABC$ meets its incircle $\omega$ at $K,L$. The parallels to $BC$ through $K,L$ meet $\omega$ again at $X,Y$, respectively. If $P=AX\cap BC$ and $Q=AY\cap BC$, prove that $BP=CQ$.
isl:2005:G6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2005:G6.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2005 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2005:G7.text:
In an acute triangle $ABC$, take $D,E,F$ as the perpendicular projections of $A,B,C$ onto $BC,CA,AB$. Take $P,Q,R$ as the perpendicular projections of $A,B,C$ onto $EF,FD,DE$, respectively. Writing $p(T)$ for the perimeter of a triangle $T$, prove that
$$p(ABC)\,p(PQR)\geq p(DEF)^2.$$
isl:2005:G7.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.
isl:2005:G7.sourceLabel: The IMO Compendium: 2005 shortlist reproduction; not a direct organizer booklet

isl:2006:G1.text:
Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$. An interior point $P$ satisfies
$$\angle PBA+\angle PCA=\angle PBC+\angle PCB.$$
Prove that $AP\geq AI$, with equality exactly when $P=I$.
isl:2006:G1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2006:G10.text: For every side $a$ of a convex polygon, let $s_a$ be the greatest area of a triangle contained in the polygon and having $a$ as a side. Prove that $\sum_a s_a$ is at least twice the area of the polygon.
isl:2006:G10.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2006:G2.text: A trapezoid $ABCD$ has parallel sides $AB>CD$. Choose $K\in AB$ and $L\in CD$ with $AK/KB=DL/LC$. Suppose $P,Q$ on segment $KL$ satisfy $\angle APB=\angle BCD$ and $\angle CQD=\angle ABC$. Prove that $P,Q,B,C$ lie on a circle.
isl:2006:G2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2006:G3.text:
In a convex pentagon $ABCDE$, suppose
$$\angle BAC=\angle CAD=\angle DAE,\qquad \angle ABC=\angle ACD=\angle ADE.$$
If $P=BD\cap CE$, prove that line $AP$ passes through the midpoint of $CD$.
isl:2006:G3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2006:G4.text: Triangle $ABC$ satisfies $\angle C<\angle A<90^\circ$. Choose $D$ on side $AC$ with $BD=BA$. The incircle of $ABC$ touches $AB,AC$ at $K,L$, respectively, and $J$ is the incenter of $BCD$. Prove that $KL$ meets segment $AJ$ at its midpoint.
isl:2006:G4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2006:G5.text: The excircle of triangle $ABC$ opposite $A$, with center $J$, touches $BC$ at $A_1$ and the extensions of $AC,AB$ at $B_1,C_1$, respectively. Suppose $A_1B_1$ is perpendicular to $AB$, and put $D=A_1B_1\cap AB$. Let $E$ be the perpendicular projection of $C_1$ onto $DJ$. Determine $\angle BEA_1$ and $\angle AEB_1$.
isl:2006:G5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2006:G6.text: Circles $\omega_1,\omega_2$, centered at $O_1,O_2$, touch externally at $D$ and touch a circle $\omega$ internally at $E,F$, respectively. Let $t$ be their common tangent at $D$. Choose the diameter $AB$ of $\omega$ perpendicular to $t$, labeled so that $A,E,O_1$ lie on the same side of $t$. Prove that $AO_1,BO_2,EF,t$ are concurrent.
isl:2006:G6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2006:G7.text: In triangle $ABC$, let $M_a,M_b,M_c$ be the midpoints of $BC,CA,AB$. Let $T_a,T_b,T_c$ be the midpoints of the circumcircle arcs $BC,CA,AB$ not containing the opposite vertices. For $i\in\{a,b,c\}$, let $\omega_i$ have diameter $M_iT_i$. For $\{i,j,k\}=\{a,b,c\}$, choose the common external tangent $p_i$ of $\omega_j,\omega_k$ which separates $\omega_i$ from those two circles. Prove that $p_a,p_b,p_c$ form a triangle similar to $ABC$, and determine the similarity ratio.
isl:2006:G7.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2006:G8.text:
Inside a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$, two circles touch externally at $P$; one passes through $A,D$ and the other through $B,C$. Suppose
$$\angle PAB+\angle PDC\leq90^\circ,\qquad\angle PBA+\angle PCD\leq90^\circ.$$
Prove that $AB+CD\geq BC+AD$.
isl:2006:G8.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2006:G9.text:
Choose $A_1,B_1,C_1$ on sides $BC,CA,AB$ of triangle $ABC$. The circumcircles of $AB_1C_1,BC_1A_1,CA_1B_1$ meet the circumcircle of $ABC$ again at $A_2
e A,B_2
e B,C_2
e C$, respectively. Reflect $A_1,B_1,C_1$ in the midpoints of $BC,CA,AB$ to obtain $A_3,B_3,C_3$. Prove that triangles $A_2B_2C_2$ and $A_3B_3C_3$ are similar.
isl:2006:G9.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2007:G1.text: In triangle $ABC$, the bisector of $\angle C$ meets the circumcircle again at $R$, and meets the perpendicular bisectors of $BC,CA$ at $P,Q$, respectively. If $S,T$ are the midpoints of $BC,CA$, prove that triangles $RQT$ and $RPS$ have equal areas.
isl:2007:G1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2007:G2.text: Let $AB=AC$ in triangle $ABC$, and let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. A point $X$ varies on the shorter arc $MA$ of the circumcircle of $ABM$. Choose $T$ inside the angle region $BMA$ so that $\angle TMX=90^\circ$ and $TX=BX$. Prove that $\angle MTB-\angle CTM$ is independent of $X$.
isl:2007:G2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2007:G3.text: A trapezoid $ABCD$ has $BC\parallel AD$, and its diagonals meet at $P$. A point $Q$ lies between the parallel lines $BC,AD$, satisfies $\angle AQD=\angle CQB$, and is separated from $P$ by line $CD$. Prove that $\angle BQP=\angle DAQ$.
isl:2007:G3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2007:G4.text: Suppose $ABCD$ is a parallelogram and $BCED$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. A line $\ell$ through $A$ meets segment $DC$ at $F$ and line $BC$ at $G$. If $EF=EG=EC$, prove that $\ell$ bisects $\angle DAB$.
isl:2007:G4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2007:G5.text: For a fixed triangle $ABC$, let $A_1,B_1,C_1$ be the midpoints of $BC,CA,AB$. A point $P$ varies on the circumcircle. Lines $PA_1,PB_1,PC_1$ meet this circle again at $A',B',C'$, respectively. Assume the six points $A,B,C,A',B',C'$ are distinct and that $AA',BB',CC'$ form a triangle. Prove that its area does not depend on $P$.
isl:2007:G5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2007:G6.text: Find the least positive real number $k$ such that the following holds for every convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ and every choice of $A_1\in AB$, $B_1\in BC$, $C_1\in CD$, $D_1\in DA$. Let $S$ be the sum of the two smallest areas among triangles $AA_1D_1,BB_1A_1,CC_1B_1,DD_1C_1$, and let $S_1$ be the area of $A_1B_1C_1D_1$. Then $kS_1\geq S$.
isl:2007:G6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2007:G7.text: An acute triangle $ABC$ has angles $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ at $A,B,C$, with $\beta>\gamma$. Let $I$ be its incenter, $R$ its circumradius, and $D$ the foot of the altitude from $A$. Choose $K$ on line $AD$ so that $AK=2R$ and $D$ lies between $A,K$. Lines $DI,KI$ meet sides $AC,BC$ at $E,F$, respectively. Prove that $IE=IF$ implies $\beta\leq3\gamma$.
isl:2007:G7.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2007:G8.text: Let $P$ lie on side $AB$ of a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$. The incircle $\omega$ of $CPD$, with center $I$, is tangent to the incircles of $APD,BPC$ at $K,L$, respectively. Put $E=AC\cap BD$ and $F=AK\cap BL$. Prove that $E,I,F$ are collinear.
isl:2007:G8.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2008:G1.text: Let $H$ be the orthocenter of an acute triangle $ABC$, and let $A_0,B_0,C_0$ be the midpoints of $BC,CA,AB$. The circles centered at $A_0,B_0,C_0$ and passing through $H$ meet the respective lines $BC,CA,AB$ at $A_1,A_2$; $B_1,B_2$; and $C_1,C_2$. Prove that these six intersection points lie on one circle.
isl:2008:G1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2008:G2.text: In a trapezoid $ABCD$ with $AB\parallel CD$, choose $E$ on line $BC$ outside segment $BC$ and $F$ inside segment $AD$ so that $\angle DAE=\angle CBF$. Put $I=CD\cap EF$ and $J=AB\cap EF$. Let $K$ be the midpoint of $EF$, and assume $K$ is not on line $AB$. Prove that $I$ lies on the circumcircle of $ABK$ if and only if $K$ lies on the circumcircle of $CDJ$.
isl:2008:G2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2008:G3.text: Points $P,Q$ lie inside a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ so that $PQDA$ and $QPBC$ are cyclic quadrilaterals. Suppose some $E$ on segment $PQ$ satisfies $\angle PAE=\angle QDE$ and $\angle PBE=\angle QCE$. Prove that $ABCD$ is cyclic.
isl:2008:G3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2008:G4.text: In an acute triangle $ABC$, let $BE$ and $CF$ be altitudes. Two circles through $A,F$ touch line $BC$ at $P,Q$, respectively; label them so that $B$ lies between $C$ and $Q$. Prove that $PE$ and $QF$ meet on the circumcircle of $AEF$.
isl:2008:G4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2008:G5.text: Let $0\leq k\leq n-2$ be integers. A set $L$ consists of $n$ lines in the plane, with no parallel pair and no three concurrent. Let $I$ be their set of intersection points, and take $O$ on none of the lines. Color $X\in I$ red when the open segment $OX$ meets at most $k$ lines of $L$. Prove that at least $\tfrac12(k+1)(k+2)$ points of $I$ are red.
isl:2008:G5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2008:G6.text:
Prove that a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ has an interior point $P$ satisfying
$$\angle PAB+\angle PDC=\angle PBC+\angle PAD=\angle PCD+\angle PBA=\angle PDA+\angle PCB=90^\circ$$
if and only if $AC\perp BD$.
isl:2008:G6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2008:G7.text: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $AB\ne BC$, and let $\omega_1,\omega_2$ be the incircles of $ABC,ADC$. Suppose a circle $\omega$ is inscribed in $\angle ABC$ and is tangent to the extensions of $AD$ and $CD$. Prove that the common external tangents of $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$ meet on $\omega$.
isl:2008:G7.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the complete printed statement.

isl:2009:G1.text: In a triangle $ABC$ with $AB=AC$, the bisectors of angles $A$ and $B$ meet $BC$ and $AC$ at $D$ and $E$, respectively. Let $K$ be the incenter of triangle $ADC$. If $\angle BEK=45^\circ$, find all possible values of $\angle BAC$.
isl:2009:G1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2009:G2.text: Let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $ABC$. Choose $P$ and $Q$ in the interiors of sides $CA$ and $AB$, respectively. Let $k$ be the circle through the midpoints of $BP,CQ,PQ$. Prove that if $PQ$ is tangent to $k$, then $OP=OQ$.
isl:2009:G2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2009:G3.text: The incircle of triangle $ABC$ touches $AB$ at $Z$ and $AC$ at $Y$. Put $G=BY\cap CZ$. Choose $R$ and $S$ so that $BCYR$ and $BCSZ$ are parallelograms. Prove that $GR=GS$.
isl:2009:G3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2009:G4.text: In a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, let $E=AC\cap BD$ and $F=AD\cap BC$. Let $G$ and $H$ be the midpoints of $AB$ and $CD$, respectively. Prove that $EF$ is tangent at $E$ to the circle through $E,G,H$.
isl:2009:G4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2009:G5.text:
Let $P$ be a convex polygon centrally symmetric about a point $O$. Prove that there is a parallelogram $R$ containing $P$ such that
$$\frac{|R|}{|P|}\leq\sqrt2,$$
where $|R|$ and $|P|$ denote their areas.
isl:2009:G5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2009:G6.text: In a quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $AB$ not parallel to $CD$, the lines $AD$ and $BC$ meet at $P$. Let $O_1,O_2$ and $H_1,H_2$ be the circumcenters and orthocenters of triangles $ABP$ and $DCP$, respectively. Let $E_1,E_2$ be the midpoints of $O_1H_1$ and $O_2H_2$. Prove that the perpendicular from $E_1$ to $CD$, the perpendicular from $E_2$ to $AB$, and the line $H_1H_2$ are concurrent.
isl:2009:G6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2009:G7.text: Let $I$ be the incenter of triangle $ABC$, and let $X,Y,Z$ be the incenters of triangles $BIC,CIA,AIB$, respectively. Prove that if $XYZ$ is equilateral, then $ABC$ is equilateral.
isl:2009:G7.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2009:G8.text: Let $ABCD$ be a circumscribed quadrilateral. A line $g$ through $A$ meets segment $BC$ at $M$ and line $CD$ at $N$. Let $I_1,I_2,I_3$ be the incenters of triangles $ABM,MNC,NDA$, respectively. Prove that the orthocenter of triangle $I_1I_2I_3$ lies on $g$.
isl:2009:G8.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2010:G1.text: In an acute triangle $ABC$, let $D,E,F$ be the feet of the altitudes on $BC,CA,AB$, respectively. Choose either intersection $P$ of line $EF$ with the circumcircle of $ABC$, and let $Q=BP\cap DF$. Prove that $AP=AQ$.
isl:2010:G1.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2010:G2.text: Let $P$ be an interior point of triangle $ABC$. The lines $AP,BP,CP$ meet its circumcircle again at $K,L,M$, respectively. The tangent to the circumcircle at $C$ meets line $AB$ at $S$. Prove that $SC=SP$ if and only if $MK=ML$.
isl:2010:G2.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2010:G3.text:
Let $A_1A_2\dots A_n$ be a convex polygon. An interior point $P$ has perpendicular projections $P_1,\dots,P_n$ on the lines $A_1A_2,\dots,A_nA_1$, respectively, and each projection lies on the corresponding side. For arbitrary points $X_1,\dots,X_n$ on those respective sides, prove that
$$\max\left\{\frac{X_1X_2}{P_1P_2},\dots,\frac{X_nX_1}{P_nP_1}\right\}\geq1.$$
isl:2010:G3.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2010:G4.text:
Let $I$ be the incenter and $\Gamma$ the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Line $AI$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $D\ne A$. Choose $F$ on side $BC$ and $E$ on arc $BDC$ so that
$$\angle BAF=\angle CAE<\tfrac12\angle BAC.$$
Let $G$ be the midpoint of $IF$. Prove that lines $DG$ and $EI$ intersect on $\Gamma$.
isl:2010:G4.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2010:G5.text: Let $ABCDE$ be a convex pentagon satisfying $BC\parallel AE$, $AB=BC+AE$ and $\angle ABC=\angle CDE$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $CE$, and let $O$ be the circumcenter of triangle $BCD$. If $\angle DMO=90^\circ$, prove that $2\angle BDA=\angle CDE$.
isl:2010:G5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2010:G6.text: An equilateral triangle $XYZ$ has its vertices $X,Y,Z$ on the sides $BC,CA,AB$, respectively, of an acute-angled triangle $ABC$. Prove that the incenter of $ABC$ lies inside triangle $XYZ$.
isl:2010:G6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2010:G7.text:
Three circular arcs $\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3$ join points $A$ and $C$ in the same half-plane bounded by $AC$, with $\gamma_2$ between $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_3$. Let $B$ lie on segment $AC$. Three rays $h_1,h_2,h_3$ start at $B$ in that half-plane, with $h_2$ between $h_1$ and $h_3$. Put $V_{ij}=h_i\cap\gamma_j$ for $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$.

For $i,j\in\{1,2\}$, let $Q_{ij}$ be the curved quadrilateral with successive vertices $V_{ij},V_{i+1,j},V_{i+1,j+1},V_{i,j+1}$, whose sides are the two corresponding ray segments and two corresponding circular arcs. Call it circumscribed if a circle touches all four of these sides.

Prove that if $Q_{11},Q_{12},Q_{21}$ are circumscribed, then $Q_{22}$ is also circumscribed.
isl:2010:G7.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2011:G6.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB=AC$, and let $D$ be the midpoint of $AC$. The bisector of $\angle BAC$ meets the circle through $D,B,C$ at a point $E$ inside $ABC$. Line $BD$ meets the circle through $A,E,B$ at $B$ and $F$. Let $I=AF\cap BE$ and $K=CI\cap BD$. Prove that $I$ is the incenter of triangle $KAB$.
isl:2011:G6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2011:G8.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with circumcircle $\omega$, and let $t$ be a tangent to $\omega$. Reflect $t$ in $BC$, $CA$ and $AB$ to obtain the lines $t_a$, $t_b$ and $t_c$, respectively. Prove that the circumcircle of the triangle formed by $t_a,t_b,t_c$ is tangent to $\omega$.
isl:2011:G8.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2013:G5.text:
Let $ABCDEF$ be a convex hexagon with $AB=DE$, $BC=EF$ and $CD=FA$, such that
$$\angle A-\angle D=\angle C-\angle F=\angle E-\angle B.$$
Prove that the diagonals $AD$, $BE$ and $CF$ are concurrent.
isl:2013:G5.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2015:G8.text:
A triangulation of a convex polygon $\Pi$ partitions it into triangles using diagonals that have no common points except vertices of the polygon. Call it a Thaiangulation if all its triangles have equal area.

Prove that any two distinct Thaiangulations of $\Pi$ differ by exactly two triangles: replacing one pair of triangles in the first with a different pair produces the second.
isl:2015:G8.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2017:G6.text: Let $n\geq3$ be an integer, and let $A$ and $B$ be two regular $n$-gons in the plane. Prove that the vertices of $A$ lying inside $B$ or on its boundary are consecutive. Equivalently, prove that a line separates these vertices from the other vertices of $A$.
isl:2017:G6.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

isl:2017:G8.text:
There are $2017$ mutually external circles on a blackboard. No two circles are tangent, and no three have a common tangent. A tangent segment joins two points of tangency on a common tangent to two circles.

Luciano draws tangent segments one at a time. Each new segment must avoid every other circle and every previously drawn tangent segment. He continues until no further tangent segment can be drawn. Find all possible numbers of tangent segments at that moment.
isl:2017:G8.transcription: Mathematically equivalent wording and normalized LaTeX; checked against the supplied official statement.

rmm:2008:1.text: Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle, and let $P$ vary inside it. Its perpendicular distances to the sides are $a^2,b^2,c^2$, where $a,b,c$ are positive real numbers. Find the locus of points $P$ for which $a,b,c$ can be the side lengths of a nondegenerate triangle.
rmm:2008:1.sourceLabel: UK competition-team archive reproduction of the RMM contest paper
rmm:2008:1.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.
rmm:2008:1.sourceCaveat: The original paper preserved by the UK team is used. Its separately labelled clarified version has the same Problem 1 formulation.

rmm:2009:3.text:
Given four points $A_1,A_2,A_3,A_4$ in the plane, no three collinear, suppose that
$$A_1A_2\cdot A_3A_4=A_1A_3\cdot A_2A_4=A_1A_4\cdot A_2A_3.$$
Let $O_i$ be the circumcentre of the triangle formed by the other three points. Assuming $A_i\ne O_i$ for every $i$, prove that the four lines $A_iO_i$ are concurrent or parallel.
rmm:2009:3.sourceLabel: UK competition-team archive reproduction of the RMM contest paper
rmm:2009:3.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2010:3.text: Let $A_1A_2A_3A_4$ be a convex quadrilateral with no pair of parallel sides. For $i=1,2,3,4$, let $\omega_i$ be the circle touching the quadrilateral externally and tangent to the lines $A_{i-1}A_i$, $A_iA_{i+1}$, and $A_{i+1}A_{i+2}$, with indices read modulo $4$. Let $T_i$ be its point of tangency with side $A_iA_{i+1}$. Prove that $A_1A_2,A_3A_4,T_2T_4$ are concurrent if and only if $A_2A_3,A_4A_1,T_1T_3$ are concurrent.
rmm:2010:3.sourceLabel: UK competition-team archive reproduction of the RMM contest paper
rmm:2010:3.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2010:5.text:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. A set $K$ of points with integer coordinates in the plane is connected if, for every $R,S\in K$, there are a positive integer $\ell$ and points $R=T_0,T_1,\ldots,T_\ell=S$ in $K$ such that consecutive points are distance $1$ apart. Define
$$\Delta(K)=\{\overrightarrow{RS}:R,S\in K\}.$$
What is the maximum value of $|\Delta(K)|$ over all connected sets $K$ of $2n+1$ points with integer coordinates in the plane?
rmm:2010:5.sourceLabel: UK competition-team archive reproduction of the RMM contest paper
rmm:2010:5.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.
rmm:2010:5.sourceCaveat: Statement collection only; the previously pending proof assessment remains separate.

rmm:2011:3.text: A triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in a circle $\omega$. A variable line $\ell$ parallel to $BC$ meets segments $AB,AC$ at $D,E$, respectively, and meets $\omega$ at $K,L$, with $D$ between $K$ and $E$. Circle $\gamma_1$ is tangent to segments $KD,BD$ and to $\omega$, while circle $\gamma_2$ is tangent to segments $LE,CE$ and to $\omega$. Determine the locus, as $\ell$ varies, of the intersection of the common inner tangents to $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$.
rmm:2011:3.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2012:2.text: Given a nonisosceles triangle $ABC$, let $D,E,F$ be the midpoints of $BC,CA,AB$, respectively. Circle $BCF$ and line $BE$ meet again at $P$, and circle $ABE$ and line $AD$ meet again at $Q$. Lines $DP,FQ$ meet at $R$. Prove that the centroid $G$ of $ABC$ lies on the circle $PQR$.
rmm:2012:2.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2012:6.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with incentre $I$ and circumcentre $O$. Let $\omega_A$ be the circle through $B,C$ tangent to the incircle of $ABC$, and define $\omega_B,\omega_C$ similarly. Circles $\omega_B,\omega_C$ meet at a point $A'$ distinct from $A$; define $B',C'$ similarly. Prove that $AA',BB',CC'$ are concurrent at a point on line $IO$.
rmm:2012:6.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2013:3.text: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle $\omega$. Lines $AB,CD$ meet at $P$, lines $AD,BC$ meet at $Q$, and diagonals $AC,BD$ meet at $R$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of segment $PQ$, and let $K$ be the common point of segment $MR$ and circle $\omega$. Prove that the circumcircle of $KPQ$ and $\omega$ are tangent.
rmm:2013:3.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2013:4.text: Let $P,P'$ be two convex quadrilateral regions in the plane, each containing its boundary. Suppose that they intersect, and let $O$ belong to their intersection. Suppose that, for every line $\ell$ through $O$, the segment $\ell\cap P$ is strictly longer than $\ell\cap P'$. Can the ratio of the area of $P'$ to the area of $P$ be greater than $1.9$?
rmm:2013:4.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2015:4.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let $D$ be the point where its incircle touches side $BC$. Let $J_b,J_c$ be the incentres of $ABD,ACD$, respectively. Prove that the circumcentre of triangle $AJ_bJ_c$ lies on the bisector of $\angle BAC$.
rmm:2015:4.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2016:1.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let $D$ be an interior point of segment $BC$. Circle $ABD$ meets segment $AC$ again at an interior point $E$, and circle $ACD$ meets segment $AB$ again at an interior point $F$. Let $A'$ be the reflection of $A$ in line $BC$. Lines $A'C,DE$ meet at $P$, and lines $A'B,DF$ meet at $Q$. Prove that $AD,BP,CQ$ are concurrent or all parallel.
rmm:2016:1.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2016:5.text:
A convex hexagon $A_1B_1A_2B_2A_3B_3$ is inscribed in a circle $\Omega$ of radius $R$. The diagonals $A_1B_2,A_2B_3,A_3B_1$ concur at $X$. For $i=1,2,3$, let $\omega_i$ be the circle tangent to segments $XA_i,XB_i$ and to the arc $A_iB_i$ of $\Omega$ containing no other vertex of the hexagon, and let $r_i$ be its radius.

(a) Prove that $R\ge r_1+r_2+r_3$.

(b) If equality holds, prove that the six points where the circles $\omega_i$ touch the diagonals $A_1B_2,A_2B_3,A_3B_1$ are concyclic.
rmm:2016:5.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2017:4.text: In the Cartesian plane, let $G_1,G_2$ be the graphs of $f_1(x)=p_1x^2+q_1x+r_1$ and $f_2(x)=p_2x^2+q_2x+r_2$, where $p_1>0>p_2$. The graphs meet at distinct points $A,B$. The four tangents to $G_1,G_2$ at $A,B$ form a convex quadrilateral with an inscribed circle. Prove that $G_1,G_2$ have the same axis of symmetry.
rmm:2017:4.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2017:6.text: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral, and let $P,Q,R,S$ lie on segments $AB,BC,CD,DA$, respectively. Segments $PR,QS$ dissect $ABCD$ into four quadrilaterals, each having perpendicular diagonals. Prove that $P,Q,R,S$ are concyclic.

rmm:2018:1.text: Let $ABCD$ be a cyclic quadrilateral and let $P$ lie on side $AB$. Diagonal $AC$ meets segment $DP$ at $Q$. The parallel to $CD$ through $P$ meets the extension of side $BC$ beyond $B$ at $K$, and the parallel to $BD$ through $Q$ meets that extension beyond $B$ at $L$. Prove that the circumcircles of $BKP$ and $CLQ$ are tangent.

rmm:2018:5.text: Let $n$ be a positive integer, and fix $2n$ distinct points on a circle. Split them into $n$ pairs, and join the points in each pair by an arrow, that is, an oriented segment. The configuration is good if no two arrows cross and there are no arrows $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}$ for which $ABCD$ is a convex quadrilateral oriented clockwise. Determine the number of good configurations.

rmm:2018:6.text: Fix a circle $\Gamma$, a line $\ell$ tangent to $\Gamma$, and another circle $\Omega$ disjoint from $\ell$ such that $\Gamma$ and $\Omega$ lie on opposite sides of $\ell$. The tangents to $\Gamma$ from a variable point $X$ on $\Omega$ meet $\ell$ at $Y,Z$. Prove that, as $X$ traces $\Omega$, the circle $XYZ$ is tangent to two fixed circles.

rmm:2019:2.text: Let $ABCD$ be an isosceles trapezoid with $AB\parallel CD$. Let $E$ be the midpoint of $AC$, and let $\omega,\Omega$ be the circumcircles of $ABE,CDE$, respectively. Let $P$ be the intersection of the tangent to $\omega$ at $A$ and the tangent to $\Omega$ at $D$. Prove that $PE$ is tangent to $\Omega$.

rmm:2020:1.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with a right angle at $C$. Let $I$ be its incentre, and let $D$ be the foot of the altitude from $C$ to $AB$. The incircle $\omega$ is tangent to $BC,CA,AB$ at $A_1,B_1,C_1$, respectively. Let $E,F$ be the reflections of $C$ in lines $C_1A_1,C_1B_1$, respectively, and let $K,L$ be the reflections of $D$ in these same lines, respectively. Prove that the circumcircles of $A_1EI$, $B_1FI$, and $C_1KL$ have a common point.

rmm:2020:1.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2021:1.text: Let $T_1,T_2,T_3,T_4$ be pairwise distinct collinear points, with $T_2$ between $T_1$ and $T_3$, and $T_3$ between $T_2$ and $T_4$. Let $\omega_1$ be a circle through $T_1,T_4$; let $\omega_2$ be the circle through $T_2$ internally tangent to $\omega_1$ at $T_1$; let $\omega_3$ be the circle through $T_3$ externally tangent to $\omega_2$ at $T_2$; and let $\omega_4$ be the circle through $T_4$ externally tangent to $\omega_3$ at $T_3$. A line crosses $\omega_1$ at $P,W$, $\omega_2$ at $Q,R$, $\omega_3$ at $S,T$, and $\omega_4$ at $U,V$, with these points in the order $P,Q,R,S,T,U,V,W$. Prove that $PQ+TU=RS+VW$.

rmm:2021:6.text:
Initially, a nonconstant polynomial $S(x)$ with real coefficients is written on a board. Whenever the board contains a polynomial $P(x)$, one may write any polynomial $P(C+x)$ or $C+P(x)$ on the board, where $C$ is a real constant. If the board contains two not necessarily distinct polynomials $P(x),Q(x)$, one may also write $P(Q(x))$ and $P(x)+Q(x)$. No polynomial is ever erased.

For finite sets $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}$ and $B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_n\}$ of real numbers, a real polynomial $f$ is $(A,B)$-nice if $f(A)=B$, where $f(A)=\{f(a_i):1\le i\le n\}$.

Determine all initial polynomials $S(x)$ for which, for any two finite sets $A,B$ of real numbers with $|A|=|B|$, an $(A,B)$-nice polynomial can be produced in finitely many steps.
rmm:2021:6.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2023:4.text: Given an acute triangle $ABC$, let $H$ and $O$ be its orthocentre and circumcentre, respectively. Let $K$ be the midpoint of segment $AH$. Let $\ell$ be a line through $O$, and let $P,Q$ be the orthogonal projections of $B,C$ onto $\ell$, respectively. Prove that $KP+KQ\ge BC$.
rmm:2023:4.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2024:5.text: Let $BC$ be a fixed segment in the plane, and let $A$ vary over points not on line $BC$. Distinct points $X$ and $Y$ are chosen on rays $\overrightarrow{CA}$ and $\overrightarrow{BA}$, respectively, such that $\angle CBX=\angle YCB=\angle BAC$. The tangents to the circumcircle of $ABC$ at $B$ and $C$ meet line $XY$ at $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Assume that $X,P,Y,Q$ are pairwise distinct and lie on the same side of $BC$. Let $\Omega_1$ be the circle through $X,P$ whose centre lies on $BC$, and let $\Omega_2$ be the circle through $Y,Q$ whose centre lies on $BC$. Prove that $\Omega_1$ and $\Omega_2$ intersect at two fixed points as $A$ varies.
rmm:2024:5.transcription: Full statement matched to the printed paper; normalized LaTeX and mathematically equivalent wording. No proof review claimed.

rmm:2025:5.text: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB<AC$, and let $H$ and $O$ be its orthocentre and circumcentre, respectively. Let $\Gamma$ be the circumcircle of triangle $BOC$. Circle $\Gamma$ intersects line $AO$ at $O$ and $A'$, and intersects the circle with centre $A$ and radius $AO$ at $O$ and $F$. Prove that the circle with diameter $AA'$, the circumcircle of triangle $AFH$, and $\Gamma$ pass through a common point.

rmm:2026:5.text:
Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AB<AC$, let $O$ be its circumcentre, and let $XYZT$ be a parallelogram inside triangle $ABC$ such that
$$\angle AXB=\angle AZC,\qquad \angle AZB=\angle AXC,$$
$$\angle AYB=\angle ATC,\qquad \angle ATB=\angle AYC.$$
Prove that the diagonals $XZ$ and $YT$ of the parallelogram intersect on the circumcircle of $BOC$.
